evidence.claim: Turkish warplanes struck Kurdish militant bases in Syria and Iraq, destroying 89 targets, in retaliation for the Istanbul bombing.
evidence.title: Turkish air strikes target Kurdish militants in Syria, Iraq after bomb attack
evidence.excerpt: Turkish warplanes struck Kurdish militant bases in Syria and Iraq, destroying 89 targets, in retaliation for the Istanbul bombing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch reproduced by Euronews with a precise date and event details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's government and security posture, though the immediate operational order came through the defense ministry.
contrary_evidence: Ankara framed the strikes as counterterrorism and retaliation.
This is conventional escalation, not nuclear escalation.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said Turkey's air operations in northern Syria were only the beginning and that a land operation would be launched when convenient.
evidence.title: Erdogan says Turkey will launch Syria land operation when convenient
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said Turkey's air operations in northern Syria were only the beginning and that a land operation would be launched when convenient.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch reproduced by Euronews, giving a direct quote from Erdoğan and the date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Erdoğan statement, relevant as a ruler-attributed escalation signal.
contrary_evidence: The stated rationale was border security and counterterrorism.
It still reflects escalation risk, not de-escalation.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan, Niinistö and Andersson agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns, paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.title: Türkiye, Finland, and Sweden sign agreement paving the way for Finnish and Swedish NATO membership
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan, Niinistö and Andersson agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns, paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO statement on the agreement and its diplomatic significance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan as a participating head of government in the negotiations.
contrary_evidence: This is alliance bargaining, not a pure peace settlement.
Turkey used veto leverage, so the move was cooperative but also coercive.

evidence.claim: Turkey lifted its veto over Finland and Sweden's bid to join NATO after the three nations agreed to protect each other's security, ending a weeks-long drama that tested allied unity against Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
evidence.title: Turkey lifts veto on Finland, Sweden joining NATO, clearing path for expansion
evidence.excerpt: Turkey lifted its veto over Finland and Sweden's bid to join NATO after the three nations agreed to protect each other's security, ending a weeks-long drama that tested allied unity against Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is generally strong on fast-moving diplomacy and this piece is independently aligned with NATO's own account.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's negotiating posture, though the breakthrough was collective.
contrary_evidence: The article also emphasizes the dramatic pressure and strategic bargaining involved.
It does not show underlying peace preferences beyond this deal.

evidence.claim: Andriy Yermak said Türkiye played an important role in the Mariupol release process, that the Presidents of Ukraine and Türkiye personally reached important agreements, and that Erdoğan provided guarantees for the safe stay of the released citizens in Türkiye.
evidence.title: The success of the operation to release people from Russian captivity was facilitated by the active involvement of international partners of Ukraine - Head of the Office of the President
evidence.publisher: Official website of the President of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Andriy Yermak said Türkiye played an important role in the Mariupol release process, that the Presidents of Ukraine and Türkiye personally reached important agreements, and that Erdoğan provided guarantees for the safe stay of the released citizens in Türkiye.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official attribution from Ukraine's presidential office, with named participants and negotiation details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the September 2022 prisoner release.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes personal participation to Erdoğan, while still acknowledging multilateral negotiation.
contrary_evidence: This is a Ukrainian official account and therefore favorable to Turkey.
It shows facilitation of a humanitarian exchange, not conflict termination.

evidence.claim: Information received concerned alleged indiscriminate airstrikes by the Turkish armed forces against the Kurdistan Workers Party in civilian areas in northern Iraq, resulting in the death and injury of civilians and damage to civilian facilities.
evidence.title: Communication report and search
evidence.excerpt: Information received concerned alleged indiscriminate airstrikes by the Turkish armed forces against the Kurdistan Workers Party in civilian areas in northern Iraq, resulting in the death and injury of civilians and damage to civilian facilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary OHCHR special-procedure communication record, though it records allegations rather than a judicial finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Turkish armed forces under Erdoğan's government; operational orders are not spelled out in the communication.
contrary_evidence: This is an allegation record, not a legal finding.
Turkey would frame the strikes as counterterrorism and self-defense.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said Turkish airstrikes since November 20, 2022 were damaging populated areas and critical infrastructure across north and northeast Syria, and that at least 10 civilians were reported to have died.
evidence.title: Northeast Syria: Turkish Strikes Exacerbate Humanitarian Crisis
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said Turkish airstrikes since November 20, 2022 were damaging populated areas and critical infrastructure across north and northeast Syria, and that at least 10 civilians were reported to have died.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: HRW combines field reporting, local interviews, and specific event descriptions in a contemporary rights-focused assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Turkish state and its military campaign under Erdoğan, though tactical orders were issued through defense channels.
contrary_evidence: Turkey said the campaign targeted militants and was retaliation for the Istanbul bombing.
The report is rights-focused and not a complete military-history account.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
